title: If, and When
label: ch:pa-if-and-when
canDo: I can suppose something with a two-part condition, time one event against another, and say what something is for.

payoff.summary: The first joining words that open their clause rather than following it, and the j- family they belong to. Punjabi marks BOTH ends of a condition where English marks only the first. lai is the counterweight: it looks forward to a purpose where kyunki looks back at a cause, and unlike the j- words it FOLLOWS what it applies to, so position alone tells the reader which habit a small word belongs to.
payoff.note: Track-local concepts on an A1 node: the corpus spine stages CONNECTIVE-IF and CONDITIONAL-REAL at B1, so the canonical concept is deliberately not claimed. What A1 needs is the two-clause sentence, not the full conditional system.
